title: Lesson 10: Repentance and the Learning Circle
description: Everyone drifts. Whether through obvious rebellion or quiet self-righteousness, we all wander off the narrow road Jesus talked about. This lesson uses the story of the prodigal son and an interactive tool called The Learning Circle to walk you through the biblical rhythm of repentance and belief, showing that the Father is not waiting to punish but waiting to welcome you home.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you saw the fruit the Spirit grows in a life joined to Jesus. But real growth is not a straight line. We stumble. We wander off His narrow path, like the prodigal son who bolted for freedom and landed in the mud, or his older brother who stayed home but hardened in pride. Both sons walked away from the Father's heart. And both needed to turn back.

This lesson is not about shame. It is about grace. When sin pulls you away, whether into rebellion or self-reliance, God does not wait for you to crawl back. He is already running. And the rhythm of turning back to Him is something every follower of Jesus needs to learn, not just once, but over and over again.
The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel.

When Jesus began His public ministry, He announced it in two words: repent and believe. Two actions. One movement. You cannot have one without the other. This is the heartbeat of the Christian life, and it never stops beating. Martin Luther began his 95 Theses with this: "When our Lord and Master Jesus Christ said 'repent,' he willed the entire life of believers to be one of repentance." He was not saying you get saved over and over again. He was saying that this ongoing turning, away from trusting yourself and toward trusting God, is the posture of the whole Christian life.

blocks.alt: Two brothers and the father in the parable of the prodigal son

blocks.title: Coming to His Senses
blocks.text:
Jesus once told a story about a prodigal son who left his father, wasted everything, and ended up starving in a pigpen. Picture him there, knees in the dirt, watching the pigs eat better than he does. Then Scripture puts the moment in one quiet line:

"When he came to his senses, he said, 'How many of my father's hired servants have food to spare, and here I am starving to death!'" (Luke 15:17 NIV)

This is the turn of the whole story, before the father runs and before the robe goes on his shoulders. Just a son in the mud, finally awake, remembering who his father is. The pigpen did not save him, but it did wake him.

When he came home, his older brother stood outside the celebration, hardened in pride and convinced he had earned what the Father freely gave. Both sons were wayward in their own way, one in obvious rebellion, the other in quiet self-righteousness. The same Father waits for both.

Every drift from God turns at this same place. A quiet pause, an honest look, a remembering of who your Father is. That is where the walk home begins.
10.1 - Which son do you relate to more right now and why, the one who ran or the one who stayed and hardened?
The Learning Circle

So what do you do when you realize you have drifted? Whether you bolted like the younger son or stiffened like the older one, the gospel calls you home. The tool below is called the Learning Circle. It is a simple, biblical rhythm that helps you turn around when you have wandered off the path. When you drift, you have a choice: keep going like nothing happened, or stop and turn back. The Learning Circle walks you through that turn.
Tap "Begin" and walk slowly from drifting off to coming home.
Walking Through the Circle

First, you notice the drift. You are walking the path of Jesus, and then you veer off. Maybe it is anger that flares up, a lie you told, a habit you cannot shake, or a slow slide into self-reliance where you stop asking God for anything because you think you have it handled. Like the prodigal packing his bags, you are simply off the path. No drama, no guilt trip. Just honesty. Name it.
All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned, every one, to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.

Then you hit the turning point and enter the circle. The right side is Repent.

1) REFLECT is where you pause and let the heart feel the weight. It means you look honestly at what happened. God shines a light on the why, maybe a weakness you ignored, a lie you bought into, a pattern you have been running from. Ask yourself: Am I off the path? What pulled me away?

2) REMORSE is not beating yourself up but letting the pain do its work, because you know God wants better for you. Like the son in the pigpen realizing, "This is not who I am." Conviction hurts, but it is love waking you up.
For godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation without regret, whereas worldly grief produces death.

The left side of the circle is Believe. Believing starts with taking God at His word before you do anything else.

Trust. Receive His forgiveness. You do not have to earn your way back or wait until you feel clean. Confess your sin to Him plainly, and trust His promise:
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

3) Plan. Now repentance gets practical. Jesus said, "Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more" (John 8:11). Notice the order: mercy first, then the call. And He never meant for you to go alone. Think small and real: who can keep you accountable? What one change can you make? What is your first move tomorrow?

4) Obey. You walk it out. Humility shows up when you change, when you ask for help, when you trust that He is stronger than your mess. You do not earn grace. You receive it and let it move your feet.

Finally, you return to the path. Not at the same spot, but further along. The prodigal did not just get home; he learned his Father's character of love and acceptance. You grow too. You see where pride was hiding and where truth sets you free. Each turn through the circle brings you closer to the Father's heart. You no longer want to take advantage of His forgiveness like a spoiled child. You worship Him and want to please Him.
10.2 - As you walked through the Learning Circle, which step is hardest for you?
10.3 - Pick one area where you have drifted, and walk it around the circle in writing: reflect, remorse, trust, plan, and obey.
The Father at the Gate

Remember: the prodigal did not come home perfect. He came home broken, hungry, unsure. But that is exactly why the Father ran. Not to scold, but to cover him, feed him, restore him. Every time you drift off the path, into sin's ditch or pride's, God is not shocked. He is ready. The Learning Circle is not about fixing yourself. It is about turning back so He can show you who He really is: kind, patient, lavishing grace on the weak.
Or do you presume on the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance?

His kindness is what draws you back. Your failures do not disqualify you. They just prove you need Him more. So do not fear the drift. Fear staying there. Because each return makes you stronger, not in willpower, but in knowing you are loved anyway.

Remember the Father you met in the first lesson, running down the road. We often fail to repent not because repentance is hard, but because we forget who is waiting at the end of the road. When you remember who He is, repentance stops feeling like crawling back to a boss and starts feeling like coming home to a Father who is already running to meet you.
Growing Up from Here

As Growing Deep wraps up, remember how far you have come. In Starting (101), you took your first steps with Jesus. These ten lessons in Growing Deep (201) have been about the vertical relationship between you and God: the Father's love, your identity in Christ, the Spirit's guidance, His Word, His grace, and now learning to turn back when you wander.

Next, Growing Up (202) turns to character and family: how the life of Jesus shapes the person you are becoming, your home, and your closest relationships. After that, Growing Out (203) sends you outward on mission to the people around you. The roots go deeper as the branches grow wider. Keep turning. Keep believing. The One who began a good work in you will bring it to completion (Philippians 1:6).
Lesson 10 Review

Repent and believe is one movement, and it lasts a whole life. Whether you drift like the younger son in rebellion or like the older son in pride, the Learning Circle walks you home: notice the drift, reflect, feel godly remorse, trust His forgiveness, then plan and obey. You do not earn grace on the way back. The Father's kindness leads you to repentance, and He is already running to meet you.
In the next lesson, you begin Growing Up by learning to love the neighbors God has placed around you.
